feedback: ACCEPT. Format: all required headers present (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION); FINAL_STATES: u4 is nonempty, declared in STATES, and is the accepting success state. Labels use only the five supplied propositions plus 'else' (no invented predicates like has_ball), and syntax matches the paper's arrow format. Ordered coverage: u0→u1 (blocker_moved) →u2 (has_door_key & blocker_moved) →u3 (door_open) →u4 (target_picked_up) mirrors the environment's hard constraints (ball moved before any toggle; key required to toggle; box room reachable only through the open door). The example trace validates reachability and rewards: step 4 +0.1, step 12 +0.2 (ball clear, key picked), step 17 +0.3, step 28 +1.0; the step-19 key drop correctly avoids the trap because door_open holds, matching key_lost's event definition. Event/persistent distinction: key_lost is treated as the one-step event it is, with an absorbing failure trap u5 entered from every live state at -1.0 — this faithfully encodes 'never drop the key while the door is still closed'. Key-first play is correctly doomed: the ball blocks the only toggle cell, so the agent must drop the key while the door is closed, which is exactly the forbidden event; ball-first play completes with no trap. The conjunction on u1→u2 correctly withholds the key milestone when the ball has been re-blocked; that situation is recoverable only by violating the constraint (or stalling at 0 reward), so no legitimate progress is mis-rewarded and no false success is possible. Else self-loops exist in all six states, covering irrelevant or unlisted events (key picked alone in u0, blocker_moved re-firing in u1, key re-pickups in u3–u5). Regressions need no explicit arcs: blocker_moved lapses are absorbed by else loops, the u1→u2 conjunction re-checks the condition at the milestone step, u2/u3 cannot regress blocker_moved (hands occupied by the key), and u0 exits after the first blocker_moved, so repeated +0.1 farming is impossible. Reward safety: dense milestones (0.1/0.2/0.3) with bounded total (≤1.6), one-shot -1.0 followed by an absorbing state, no repeated penalties, no reward on else loops. Minor non-blocking notes: (u3, key_lost)→u5 is unreachable (the door cannot relock and key_lost requires a closed door) — a harmless defensive arc; (u2, key_lost) is reachable and correctly traps the only way to lose the key there. Overall semantically faithful, compact (6 states), and safe.

feedback: All five declared propositions are implemented and no extras, imports, actions, or side effects are present. blocker_moved: the full-grid scan checks, for the unique door, whether grid.get(dx-1, dy) holds a ball — equivalent to the reference single-cell check, since there is exactly one door, it always sits in the interior shared wall (x >= 2, so the x > 0 guard never skips it), and the front/start-side cell is (dx-1, dy). It is a pure current-state read: true when the ball is picked up (off-grid), true when dropped elsewhere, and correctly false again if dropped back on that cell (unlatched condition). has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the documented expressions exactly (carrying-key-with-matching-door-color, any open door, carrying-box-with-mission-color-match). key_lost: reads env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] read-only and reproduces prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D with the current-state expressions; the leading truthiness guard on the valuation dict is a harmless no-op given a complete valuation, and the event semantics are correct — no latching, true only on the single step where the key was carried at the previous step and is not carried now with the door closed. Parenthesization in key_lost is balanced and each function returns a boolean. All attribute accesses (type, color, is_open, env.carrying, env.mission, grid.get, width/height, episode_memory) are within the documented API, with None-guards before attribute reads on grid cells.
